ops.title: portable-gate misdiagnoses a deleted or renamed package as a portability regression
ops.description:
Found 2026-08-01 by the P4.3b C2 refuter. IMMEDIATELY RELEVANT: phase-4 Lane A deletes
`internal/durablefile`, which is a declared-portable package — so the very next lane hits this.

Removing a package declared in ci/portable.txt makes the gate report it as a regression:
`- ci/exportcensus` … "no longer builds and vets under GOOS=linux", with the explain block emitting
`no required module provides package github.com/yasyf/daemonkit/ci/exportcensus; to add it: go get
github.com/yasyf/daemonkit/ci/exportcensus` — actively wrong advice for an in-module package.

And the remedy is unreachable: `--write` correctly refuses the regression direction (that hardening
is deliberate and right — it stops a real regression being laundered out of the manifest with one
command), so ci/portable.txt has to be hand-edited. A deletion is not a regression and should not
share its remedy.

Related observation from the same review, presented as an observation rather than a defect:
scripts/export-census.sh:24's `--write` unconditionally regenerates ci/exported.txt from the tree, so
a symbol that vanished is silently dropped and the check goes green — the same shape the portable
gate was just hardened against. Arguably not the same class (an export removal is often a change's
intent, a portability regression is a build break), so it is recorded, not filed as a defect.

ops.text: Removing a declared package from the tree is reported as a deletion, not as 'no longer builds and vets under GOOS=linux'
The remedy the message prints is achievable (--write currently refuses, so ci/portable.txt must be hand-edited)
